### Learning R

- R for Data Science [@wickham2023r4ds] - learn data science with the tidyverse
- [R for Epidemiology](https://www.r4epi.com/) - an introduction to R, with epidemiology examples
- [The Epidemiologist R Handbook](https://epirhandbook.com/) - task-oriented reference for applied epidemiology
- [R Graphics Cookbook](https://r-graphics.org/) - recipes for common `{ggplot2}` figures
- [R for Reproducible Scientific Analysis](https://swcarpentry.github.io/r-novice-gapminder/) - Software Carpentry's introductory lesson
- [Building reproducible analytical pipelines with R](https://raps-with-r.dev/) - project-level reproducibility in R
- [Posit Recipes](https://posit.cloud/learn/recipes) - short, task-focused R code snippets

### Learning Python

- [Python Tutor](https://pythontutor.com/) - steps through a short program one line at a time
  and draws each variable and object in memory;
  it visualizes Python, Java, C, C++ and JavaScript (not R) and limits program length, so use it on small examples

### Coming to R from SAS

- [The sassy system](https://r-sassy.org/) - packages that bring familiar SAS concepts to R;
  its [`{procs}`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=procs) package
  provides versions of `proc freq`, `proc means`, `proc ttest`, `proc reg`, and other common procedures
- [R for SAS and SPSS Users](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4614-0685-3) (Muenchen) - common SAS and SPSS tasks, done in R
- [SAS and R](https://www.routledge.com/SAS-and-R-Data-Management-Statistical-Analysis-and-Graphics-Second-Edition/Kleinman-Horton/p/book/9781466584495) (Kleinman and Horton) - side-by-side SAS and R code for data management and analysis

### General R Programming

- Advanced R [@wickham2019advr] - deep dive into R programming and internals, including
  [functions](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/functions.html),
  [object-oriented systems](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/oo.html#oop-systems),
  and [debugging](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/debugging.html)
- [Debugging R code](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~swood34/RCdebug/RCdebug.html) (Simon Wood) -
  debugging R and compiled code called from R
- [Differences between the base R and `{magrittr}` pipes](https://www.tidyverse.org/blog/2023/04/base-vs-magrittr-pipe/) - how `|>` and `%>%` behave differently
- [Spatial Data Science: With Applications in R](https://r-spatial.org/book) - spatial data analysis in R

### Summary tables

- [`{gtsummary}`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/) - flexible demographics and summary tables; start here
- [`{table1}`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=table1) - HTML "Table 1" demographics tables
- [`{arsenal}`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=arsenal) - summary tables, from the Mayo Clinic
- `{procs}` (under "Coming to R from SAS" above) - SAS-style frequency and means tables

### R Package Development

- R Packages [@wickham2023rpkgs] - comprehensive guide to R package development
- Tidyverse design guide [@wickham2023tidydesign] - principles for designing R packages and APIs that are intuitive, composable, and consistent with tidyverse philosophy
- [usethis documentation](https://usethis.r-lib.org/) - workflow automation for R projects
- [devtools documentation](https://devtools.r-lib.org/) - essential development tools
- [pkgdown documentation](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/) - create package websites
- [testthat documentation](https://testthat.r-lib.org/) - unit testing framework
- [Releasing to CRAN](https://r-pkgs.org/release.html) and the
  [CRAN Cookbook](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/) - preparing a CRAN submission
  (see also [Code Publication](code-publication.qmd))
- [Contributing to R](https://contributor.r-project.org/) - getting involved with base R itself

### Shiny Development

- Mastering Shiny [@wickham2021shiny] - comprehensive guide to building web applications with Shiny
- Engineering Production-Grade Shiny Apps [@fay2021engineering] - best practices for production Shiny applications

### Git and Version Control

- Happy Git and GitHub for the useR [@bryan2023happygit] - essential guide to using Git and GitHub with R
- [Pull request helpers in `{usethis}`](https://usethis.r-lib.org/articles/pr-functions.html) - the `pr_*()` workflow from R
- [Oh Shit, Git!?!](https://ohshitgit.com/) - plain-language fixes for common Git mistakes
- [`{saperlipopette}`](https://maelle.github.io/saperlipopette/) - practice Git rescue exercises from R
- [Git Magic](http://www-cs-students.stanford.edu/~blynn/gitmagic/) - a short, free Git book
- [`{gitdown}`](https://thinkr-open.github.io/gitdown/) - R package for documenting git commit history as a bookdown report,
  organized by patterns like tags or issues
